material_definitions: The Li+ superionic argyrodites Li6PS5-xSexBr (0 <= x <= 1) were synthesized to study the effect of increased anion polarizability on ionic transport.
Rietveld refinements of XRD and neutron PDF data confirmed a cubic F-43m argyrodite structure with unit cell expansion obeying Vegard’s law.
Minor impurity phases of LiBr and Li3OBr were detected at less than 5 wt%, with negligible impact on transport properties.
Se substitution occurs on both the 4d (free chalcogenide) and 16e (PCh4 tetrahedra) sites, leading to decreased Br-/Ch2- site disorder.
The broadening of Li+ diffusion pathways and increased Li+ occupancy on the 48h site were observed with increasing Se content.

material_definitions: Se2- substitution within Li6PS5-xSexBr (0 ≤ x ≤ 1) was performed to study the effect of lattice polarizability and Br-/Ch2- exchange on lithium transport.
Structural characterization was performed using X-ray diffraction, neutron pair distribution function analysis, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy.
Increasing Se substitution leads to an increase in lattice parameters and the formation of PS3Se3- polyhedra via 16e Wyckoff position occupancy.
Structural changes induce a rearrangement of Li+ from the 24g to the 48h site and a widening of the diffusion pathways.
The study highlights that vanishing site disorder with Se substitution can counteract the beneficial effects of Li+ sublattice broadening on ionic transport.
